candidate.title: TruSeq RNA
candidate.scope: The single TruSeq RNA preparation outline in the assigned Illumina poster panel: mRNA with a terminal A-run, polyA select at a T-rich support, Fragment, Random hexamer, and First and second strand synthesis ending in double-stranded cDNA fragments. No alternative branch or kit version is named. This is the depicted early library-preparation architecture, without a claim to a complete sequencing-ready protocol or to all TruSeq RNA implementations.

states.label: Polyadenylated mRNA
features: Long purple strand labeled mRNA with a terminal AAAAA run.
The schematic does not identify an upstream specimen or total-RNA preparation.

evidence.locator: Upper long purple strand with AAAAA and mRNA label

states.label: Poly(A)-selected RNA bound at a capture support
features: Purple RNA A-run is paired with a T-run connected to a gray support icon.
Interpreted as poly(A)/oligo(dT) capture; support composition and release chemistry are unspecified.
The A/T runs are schematic end-group/attachment features, not measured tail or oligonucleotide lengths.

states.label: Double-stranded cDNA fragments

RNA-derived DNA is the depicted endpoint and library precursor; no adapters, indexes, barcodes or sequencing reads are depicted.

operations.label: polyA select
operations.description: Enrich the polyadenylated RNA target by capture at its A-rich end. The output differs from the input by its depicted association with a T-rich capture oligonucleotide attached to a support.
operations.mechanism: The drawing shows A/T pairing at a support; interpreted as support-attached oligo(dT) hybridization to RNA poly(A).
operations.information_effect: Selects a poly(A)-binding RNA population labeled mRNA. This selects by the depicted terminal feature; the drawing does not demonstrate complete recovery or perfect biological specificity.

operations.label: Fragment
operations.description: Convert the selected long RNA into shorter RNA fragments. The multiple purple segments are products within one population, not alternative workflow branches. The schematic does not resolve the capture-release interface or the fragmentation chemistry.
operations.information_effect: The material now carries portions of the selected RNA molecules rather than their intact full-length continuity.

operations.label: Random hexamer
operations.description: Associate random-hexamer primers with the RNA fragments, represented by short blue bars alongside the purple templates. The output is primed RNA suitable for the depicted downstream copying step; primer extension is included in the following strand-synthesis operation.
operations.mechanism: Random-hexamer primer association with fragment templates, inferred from the caption and primer bars; no enzyme or annealing conditions are specified.
operations.information_effect: Provides copying sites on fragment bodies, allowing RNA regions beyond the selected poly(A) end to be represented in DNA.

operations.label: First and second strand synthesis
operations.description: Copy the primed RNA fragments into first-strand cDNA and form the second DNA strand, yielding the paired blue DNA fragments shown below the arrow. The figure combines these transformations in one caption and does not expose their internal intermediates.
operations.mechanism: RNA-templated first-strand DNA synthesis followed by second-strand DNA synthesis, interpreted from the substrate, caption and double-line products; specific enzymes and RNA-removal chemistry are not identified.
operations.information_effect: Transfers sequence information from the selected RNA fragments to double-stranded DNA. The physical carrier at the endpoint is cDNA, representing selected transcript regions. The panel provides no measured readout, quantitative molecule-to-read relationship or sequencing operation.

Random-hexamer priming is a component, not an alternative method. Fragmentation and priming are distinguished as two named transformations sharing one intermediate drawing.

checks.rationale: Independent inspection finds every in-scope transformation and all eight material routes represented. Poly(A) capture, fragmentation, random-hexamer association and combined first/second-strand synthesis form one population route. The five fragment glyphs are not separate workflow branches; no multi-input/output operation, compartment, pooling or alternative is depicted. The A/T attachment is retained, its unshown release interface is acknowledged, and the unprimed boundary is explicitly inferred. The endpoint is a cDNA library precursor representing selected RNA regions, without a claim to sequencing, adapters, strand specificity, quantitative readout or a complete protocol. Only catalogue and diagram evidence is supplied; the card has no references and requires no paper association. Empty paper_matches and corrections are appropriate. No consequential unresolved question blocks this depiction-level architecture.
